claim: THBS1, F3, TAGLN, ANKRD1, and DKK1 are positive regulators of secretome PON1 fucosylation-mediated drug-resistant clone outgrowth.
source: This analysis highlighted C19orf25, RPS27L, CLDN2, PAQR3, and SOX4 as putative blockers; while THBS1, F3, TAGLN, ANKRD1, and DKK1 as positive regulators of secretome PON1 fucosylation-mediated DR clone outgrowth (Figure 6E), all of which were validated in a separate gene expression analysis (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis and qPCR validation shown in figures.

claim: Only C19orf25 is denoted as 'commonly essential' in a pan-cancer ranking scheme among the top 10 up- and down-regulated hits.
source: We observed variable pan-cancer dependency signatures among the top 10 up- and down-regulated hits from our initial screen and found that only C19orf25 is denoted as 'commonly essential' in a pan-cancer ranking scheme.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of genome-scale loss-of-function screening data from the Cancer DepMap project.

claim: Many of the top differentially expressed genes display high dependency scores in a fraction of cancer cell lines.
source: Regardless, many of these genes display high dependency scores in a fraction of cancer cell lines (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of genome-scale loss-of-function screening data shown in figures.

claim: Many of the top differentially expressed genes' dependencies strongly correlate with either a drug-sensitive or a drug-resistant state to inhibitors of EGFR or RTK signaling.
source: Indeed, many of these gene dependencies strongly correlate with either a drug-sensitive or a drug-resistant state to inhibitors of EGFR or RTK signaling, albeit varied p values mainly due to different cancer lineages screened.
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis between gene dependency and drug sensitivity data.

claim: Top overlapping up-regulated genes upon secretome de-N-glycosylation and PON1 fucosylation inhibition mostly correlates with a drug-sensitive state, while the down-regulated genes are more associated with resistance to EGFR-TKIs or RTK inhibitors.
source: Intriguingly, top overlapping up-regulated genes upon secretome de-N-glycosylation, and PON1 fucosylation inhibition mostly correlates with a drug-sensitive state, while the down-regulated genes are more associated with resistance to EGFR-TKIs or RTK inhibitors (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis between gene dependency and drug sensitivity data shown in figures.

claim: High expression of RPS27L and C19orf25 are correlated with increased first progression survival or relapse-free survival in large lung cancer patient cohorts.
source: In large LC patient cohorts, high expression of two up-regulated gene hits, RPS27L and C19orf25, are correlated with increased first progression survival or RFS, while high expression of two down-regulated gene hits, DKK1 and THBS1, are associated with poor survival outcomes after therapy (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis from patient cohorts shown in figures.

claim: High expression of DKK1 and THBS1 are associated with poor survival outcomes after therapy in large lung cancer patient cohorts.
source: In large LC patient cohorts, high expression of two up-regulated gene hits, RPS27L and C19orf25, are correlated with increased first progression survival or RFS, while high expression of two down-regulated gene hits, DKK1 and THBS1, are associated with poor survival outcomes after therapy (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis from patient cohorts shown in figures.

claim: RPS27L RNAi and DKK1 overexpression both displayed specific phenotypic responses to therapy-induced secretome de-N-glycosylation or therapy-induced secretome-specific fucosylated PON1 inhibition.
source: Predominantly, RPS27L RNAi and DKK1 overexpression both displayed specific phenotypic responses to TIS de-N-glycosylation or TIS-specific fucosylated PON1 inhibition.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi and overexpression experiments in conditioned media co-culture assays.

claim: In both modified therapy-induced secretome conditions, silencing RPS27L expression or overexpressing DKK1 promoted growth acceleration and EGFR-TKI resistance of drug-resistant clones reversing the supposed growth limitation and sensitization under such therapy-induced secretome modifications.
source: In both modified TIS conditions, silencing RPS27L expression or overexpressing DKK1 promoted growth acceleration and EGFR-TKI resistance of DR clones reversing the supposed growth limitation and sensitization under such TIS modifications (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell tracking and drug sensitivity assay data from RNAi and overexpression experiments shown in figures.

claim: Both RPS27L RNAi and DKK1 overexpression prevented senescence induction and stimulated tumor microenvironment-associated resistance genes upon de-N-glycosylation of therapy-induced secretome or inhibition of therapy-induced secretome-specific PON1 fucosylation.
source: Further, both targeted approaches prevented senescence induction and stimulated TME-associated resistance genes upon de-N-glycosylation of TIS or inhibition of TIS-specific PON1 fucosylation (Figure 6—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from RNAi and overexpression experiments shown in figures.

claim: Modulatory genes controlling drug-resistant clone response to inhibited secretome PON1 fucosylation are functionally associated with drug sensitivity to targeted therapies and are potential therapeutic targets to limit drug-resistant clone outgrowth.
source: Collectively, our data indicate that modulatory genes controlling DR clone response to inhibited secretome PON1 fucosylation are functionally associated with drug sensitivity to targeted therapies and are potential therapeutic targets to limit DR clone outgrowth.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from comprehensive experimental data showing functional roles of identified genes in drug resistance.
